title: PSG vs. Barcelona Player Ratings: Reigning Champions End Barca’s Perfect Season in Thriller
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto CasillasOct 20, 2026Fabián Ruiz (front) scored the dagger against Barcelona.  / Franck Fife/AFP/Getty ImagesIn one of the best games of the early season, reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain handed Barcelona their first defeat of the season with a brilliant 4–2 win that sends a statement of intent for the rest of European soccer: The Champions League monarchs remain the team to beat this season.
As expected, Barcelona and PSG traded blows in an end-to-end affair from the start. However, it was the hosts who looked the better side and created the most dangerous chances of the first half.

Joan García had done brilliantly to keep the game scoreless but there was nothing he could do to deny Désiré Doué’s perfectly placed shot from the edge of the box 38 minutes in following a dreadful Lamine Yamal turnover.

The second half was an absolute thriller. Xavi Espart equalized for an improved Barça 10 minutes after the restart before Lucas Hernández restored PSG’s lead with a powerful header 72 minutes in. Hansi Flick’s side responded in the 77th minute thanks to a stellar finish from Yamal.

But just when it seemed like Barcelona could complete their comeback, the reigning champions answered and Vitinha scored a wonderful goal just two minutes later. Fabián Ruiz buried the nail in Barcelona’s coffin when he strolled behind João Cancelo at the back post to tap-in an Achraf Hakimi cross.

The pair of European juggernauts delivered an epic clash on Tuesday, but in the end, Luis Enrique’s men showed Barcelona they still have plenty to improve on before they can truly challenge them for the Champions League crown.

Désiré Doué was unplayable against Barcelona.  / David Ramos/UEFA/Getty ImagesIn a game that featured some of the biggest stars in world soccer, none shone brighter than Désiré Doué. The winger scored a stellar opener, assisted his team’s second and was the best player on the pitch for his 78 minutes in the game. What a player.

PSG’s dominant midfield trio of João Neves, Vitinha and Fabián Ruiz also stole the show against Barcelona. Although the Catalans didn’t have their top-choice midfield at any point during the game, the Parisian engine room showcased why it’s considered the best in the world—even above Barça’s stellar midfield.

Xavi Espart delivered a brilliant performance on the biggest stage of his young career. The La Masia graduate was flawless defensively and scored his maiden Champions League goal. His quality was never in doubt, but he demonstrated he is also capable of producing under immense pressure.

João Cancelo had a night to forget.  / Federico Pestellini/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty ImagesBarcelona suffered defensively throughout the game, but nobody had a worse performance than João Cancelo. The fullback’s known defensive deficiencies were exploited and he completely lost Ruiz in the action that sealed the result for PSG. On the ball, he equally struggled in what was his worst performance since returning to Barcelona earlier this year.

Both Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi have had stellar starts to the year, but the pair offered next to nothing on Tuesday. On the other end, Ferran Torres failed to make an impression, missing three clear chances against his former club.

The victory took a toll on PSG, with the trio of Ousmane Dembélé, Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia exiting the pitch with injuries. For Barcelona, Dani Olmo also had to be withdrawn with an early injury.
Vitinha won the game for PSG with a rocket of a hit.  / Franco Arland/Getty Images *Ratings provided by FotMob*

GK: Matvey Safonov—6.3: Brilliantly held his ground one-on-one against Fermín López in the first half, but his positioning could’ve been much better to deny Espart’s and Yamal’s equalizers at his near-post.
RB: Achraf Hakimi—8.2: Essentially disregarded any defensive duties and spent much of the game creating in the final third, leaving Anthony Gordon for Marquinhos to mark. Assisted Ruiz’s dagger.

CB: Marquinhos—6.7: Continues to age like fine wine. He often found himself on an island against Gordon but more than held his own against the speedy winger. In the end, though, the taxing effort resulted in him leaving the pitch with a muscular issue.
CB: Willian Pacho—6.5: Put his body on the line and got kicked in the face in a heroic intervention to deny López.
LB: Lucas Hernández—8.0: Stayed tight on Yamal all game and then crowned his night with a powerful header to score PSG’s second.

CM: João Neves—8.7: After getting dropped against Manchester City last week, the diminutive midfielder looked back to his best in his return to the XI. Had a mouthwatering clash with Pedri all game. Crashed the box constantly and delivered a stellar performance overall.
